Nissan's Global Off-Roader Set To Go On 'Patrol' In The U.S. In 2027

By Elena Rostova Global Automotive Industry & Supply-Chain Analyst • via Carscoops Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Carscoops Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights

⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • ELENA ROSTOVA Global Automotive Industry & Supply-Chain Analyst

Capital Allocation Across Global Automakers

From an institutional perspective, the economic figures outlined in this dispatch from Carscoops reflect monumental shifts in automotive capital. Legacy original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and agile EV startups alike must balance heavy gigafactory capital expenditures against fluctuating consumer demand and trade tariffs. Supply chain resilience—especially across lithium, cathode precursor materials, and semiconductors—is determining profitability.

Big Picture: Upcoming quarterly delivery reports and operating margins will indicate which manufacturers are successfully navigating the EV transformation curve.

Finally, the United States gets the Patrol, even if it's technically a trim for right now

📌 The Core Development

Nissan has sold the Armada in the U.S. and the Patrol overseas for a decade, and despite the different names, they're essentially the same vehicle. Now, Nissan is bringing these two nameplates together in the U.S. with a special version of the Armada called the Patrol Pro-4X. It replaces the old Pro-4X and is the first model to use the Patrol name in America since 1969.

The new Patrol Pro-4X shares the same off-road philosophy as the outgoing Pro-4X and features the same modifications. For all intents and purposes, the two models are the same, except for the name. Nissan says it's bringing back the Patrol name to the U.S. to celebrate 75 years since the Patrol debuted in 1951. It hinted at the nameplate's return when it unveiled the wild Armada June Patrol Concept at SEMA last week .

🔍 Background & Sector Context

For Armada owners planning to take their almighty SUVs off the tarmac, the Patrol Pro-4X will be the logical choice. It comes standard with an electronically locking rear differential, a metal skid plate, and adaptive electronic air suspension. Further bolstering its off-road credentials are special 20-inch wheels with all-terrain tires and the Invisible Hood View camera that essentially allows drivers to see what's under the engine bay on the infotainment screen. This system is perfect for avoiding rocks and boulders.

For the new 2027 Armada Patrol Pro-4X, shoppers can order it with several accessories, including new Nismo rock sliders, a Nismo roof rack, and distinctive Nismo Axis wheels with BFGoodrich rubber.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

The introduction of the Patrol-branded model coincides with the launch of the full 2027 Armada family. Last year's entry-level Armada SV 4x2 has been axed, and now positioned at the base of the family is the SL 4x2, priced from $66,565, including destination and handling. This is up slightly from the $65,805 MSRP of the 2026 model. The Armada SL 4x4 sticks around for 2027 and is priced from $69,565.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

The range then steps up to the Platinum 4x4 priced from $78,065, or a hefty $2,300 increase over last year's model. Nissan has ditched the Platinum 4x2 and Platinum Reserve 4x2 models from 2026, further simplifying the range. Prices for the Patrol Pro-4X are the real headline, with it starting at $81,265. That's a significant $4,690 premium over the outgoing Pro-4X. Completing the 2027 Armada range are the $82,965 Nismo 4x4 and the Platinum Reserve 4x4, priced from $86,865.

All Armada versions use the same twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V6. In the SL, Platinum, Platinum Reserve, and Patrol Pro-4X models, this V6 delivers 425 horsepower and 516 pound-feet of torque. Fitting of its name, the Nismo 4x4 is upgraded to 460 hp . A nine-speed automatic transmission is shared across the range. Production of the new Patrol Pro-4X will start this month.
